measures.title: Increase Acre Limit for Agriculture and Timber Conservation Use Property Tax Classification Amendment
measures.summary: Increase the maximum acreage of agricultural and timber property that can be classified as bona fide conservation use property, which is taxed at 40% of the land's value, from 2,000 acres to 4,000 acres.
measures.intent: Land enrolled in Georgia's conservation use programme is taxed on its value as working farm or timber land rather than its market value, under a covenant to keep it in that use for at least ten years. One owner may currently enrol up to 2,000 acres; this amendment would raise that ceiling to 4,000. The ballot question states the purpose as protecting family farmland. A companion law, HB 90, is already signed and takes effect on January 1, 2027 only if voters ratify this amendment.
measures.opposition: No organised opposition campaign was identified as of October 16, 2026. Some legislators voted against referring the measure, and published vote tallies differ between trackers, so no count is given here; the enabling legislation's own record on legis.ga.gov is the source to check.

measures.title: Require Nonpartisan Elections for Probate Judges Amendment
measures.summary: Require that probate judges be elected on a nonpartisan basis.
measures.intent: Probate judges handle wills and estates, some marriage and firearms licences, and in many counties election administration. Every other class of Georgia judge is already elected without party labels; probate judges are the exception. This amendment would remove party labels from their races statewide.
measures.opposition: No organised opposition campaign was identified as of October 16, 2026. Some legislators voted against referring the measure, and published vote tallies differ between trackers, so no count is given here; the enabling legislation's own record on legis.ga.gov is the source to check.

measures.title: Authorize Creation of Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund Amendment
measures.summary: Allow the state legislature to create and dedicate revenue to a fund titled the Georgia Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund.
measures.intent: Georgia collects a monthly 9-1-1 fee on phone lines. This amendment would let the General Assembly put that existing revenue into a dedicated, non-lapsing fund that may only be spent on expanding, maintaining and operating 9-1-1 systems, including the move to Next Generation 9-1-1. It does not itself set or raise the fee; a future state law would decide what goes into the fund and how it is managed.
measures.opposition: No organised opposition campaign was identified as of October 16, 2026. Some legislators voted against referring the measure, and published vote tallies differ between trackers, so no count is given here; the enabling legislation's own record on legis.ga.gov is the source to check.

measures.title: Georgia Homestead Exemption for Surviving Spouses and Children of Disabled Veterans Measure
measures.summary: Extend the homestead property tax exemption to the surviving spouses and minor children of disabled veterans.
measures.statusNote: Not on the November 3, 2026 ballot. HB 52 passed the House 170-5 on March 6, 2025; the Senate adopted a substitute 50-0 on April 2, 2026, which returned the bill to the House, and the House did not act on that substitute before the General Assembly adjourned. A property-tax exemption must clear both chambers in the same form and be signed before it can be referred to voters, so this measure was never referred and will not appear on a ballot this cycle. Kept as a record of what was proposed.
measures.intent: Georgia exempts part of the assessed value of a disabled veteran's home from property tax. HB 52 would have extended that exemption to an un-remarried surviving spouse and to minor children, and allowed it to carry to a later home in the state. It was never referred to voters, so there is nothing to vote on.

enablingLegislation.title: Georgia Homestead Exemption for Surviving Spouses and Children of Disabled Veterans
